record.field: To ensure all visitors are properly screened, registered, and authorized before granting access to the premises.
Applies to all guard posts with visitor reception duties at building entrances, lobbies, and reception areas.

Purpose

This SOP establishes standardized procedures for processing visitor access requests, conducting security screening, and maintaining visitor logs in compliance with SIRA requirements.

Responsibilities

  • Security Guard: Execute visitor screening and registration
  • Supervisor: Monitor compliance and handle escalations
  • Control Room: Verify visitor credentials when required

Required Equipment

  • Visitor Management System (computer/tablet)
  • ID scanner or camera
  • Visitor badges
  • Logbook (backup)
  • Metal detector (if applicable)

• Stand and greet the visitor with "Good [morning/afternoon/evening], welcome to [location name]"
  • Maintain professional posture and eye contact
  • Speak clearly in English; use Arabic if visitor prefers
  • Smile and create positive first impression
Always maintain awareness of surroundings while greeting visitors. Do not turn your back to the entrance.

• Politely request: "May I please see your Emirates ID or passport?"
  • Accept only original government-issued photo ID (no copies)
  • Verify photo matches the person presenting ID
  • Check ID expiration date - reject expired IDs
  • Look for signs of tampering or forgery

Acceptable IDs: Emirates ID, Passport, GCC National ID, UAE Driving License
Never accept photocopies or digital images of IDs. If ID appears fake or tampered, immediately notify supervisor and politely detain person.

• Search visitor name in GuardLink watchlist system
  • Check for any active bans or restrictions
  • Verify against previous incident reports
  • If match found: Follow escalation procedure (do NOT grant access)
  • If no match: Proceed to next step
CRITICAL: Never inform the visitor they are on a watchlist. Immediately call supervisor using code phrase "Code Blue verification needed."

• Ask: "What is the purpose of your visit?"
  • Ask: "Who are you visiting?" (Get name, unit/office number)
  • Check if visitor has appointment/pre-registration
  • Call host to confirm visitor is expected
  • Wait for host confirmation before proceeding

If host doesn't answer:

  • Try alternate contact number
  • Check with building management
  • Offer visitor to wait in designated area
  • Do NOT allow access without confirmation

• Ask visitor to place bags/items on X-ray scanner (if available)
  • Request visitor to walk through metal detector
  • If alarm sounds: Conduct courteous hand-held metal detector scan
  • Visually inspect bags - look for prohibited items
  • If suspicious items found: Politely deny entry and call supervisor

Prohibited Items: Weapons, explosives, illegal drugs, flammable materials, recording devices (if restricted by site policy)
Never physically search a person. Use metal detector only. For pat-down searches, call same-gender supervisor.

• Open GuardLink Visitor Management module
  • Click "New Visitor Registration"
  • Scan or manually enter Emirates ID number
  • Fill in all required fields: Name, ID Number, Contact, Purpose, Host
  • Take visitor photo using webcam/camera
  • Generate visitor badge with QR code
  • Print visitor badge
Issue Visitor Badge and Grant Access

• Hand visitor badge to guest
  • Instruct: "Please wear this badge visibly at all times"
  • Return original ID to visitor
  • Provide directions to destination
  • Inform visitor of any restrictions (smoking areas, photography, etc.)
  • Note entry time in system
  • Unlock/open access control barrier

• When visitor returns, greet and thank them for visiting
  • Collect visitor badge
  • Scan badge or manually close visitor record in system
  • Note exit time
  • Ask if they need any assistance (taxi, directions, etc.)
  • Wish them a good day
To ensure safe and effective response to fire emergencies, prioritizing life safety and property protection.
Applies to all security personnel. Mandatory training required annually.

Purpose

This SOP defines the immediate response actions for fire emergencies in accordance with UAE Civil Defense regulations and SIRA safety standards.

Fire Response Priority

  1. LIFE SAFETY - Protect and evacuate people
  2. ALERT - Notify emergency services and management
  3. CONTAIN - Prevent fire spread if safe to do so
  4. EVACUATE - Complete building evacuation

CRITICAL SAFETY RULES

  • NEVER put yourself in danger to save property
  • NEVER use elevators during fire emergency
  • NEVER re-enter building until Civil Defense gives all-clear
  • ALWAYS prioritize human life over property

• Fire alarm sounding
  • Visible smoke or flames
  • Smell of burning materials
  • Report from occupants
  • Fire detection system alert

DO NOT IGNORE any fire indication. Treat all alarms as real until confirmed otherwise.
Never assume fire alarm is false. Every second counts in fire emergency.

IMMEDIATELY CALL 997 (Civil Defense)

Provide clear information:

  • "Fire emergency at [exact address]"
  • Building name and number
  • Floor and location of fire
  • Size of fire (small/medium/large)
  • Any trapped persons
  • Your name and callback number

THEN notify:

  • Control room/security supervisor (radio)
  • Building management
  • Press manual fire alarm pull station
ALWAYS call 997 first, even if fire seems small. Do not wait for supervisor approval.

• Shout loudly: "FIRE! EVACUATE NOW! USE STAIRS!"
  • Direct people to nearest emergency exit
  • Help elderly, disabled, children first
  • Knock on doors shouting "FIRE! EVACUATE!"
  • Check restrooms and common areas quickly
  • Ensure people do NOT use elevators
  • Tell people to leave belongings and GO
Spend maximum 5 minutes on immediate area evacuation. Do not endanger yourself searching entire building.
ASSESS - Evaluate Fire Size and Safety

SMALL FIRE (Incipient):

  • Contained to small area (wastebasket, small appliance)
  • No heavy smoke
  • Exit path clear
  • Fire extinguisher immediately available
  • You are trained and confident

→ May attempt to extinguish (see Step 5)

LARGE FIRE:

  • Spreading rapidly
  • Heavy smoke/heat
  • Blocking exits
  • You are unsure or afraid

→ EVACUATE IMMEDIATELY (skip to Step 6)
When in doubt, GET OUT. No property is worth your life.
EXTINGUISH - Fight Small Fire (Only if Safe)

PASS Method for Fire Extinguisher:

  • Pull the pin
  • Aim nozzle at base of fire (not flames)
  • Squeeze handle
  • Sweep side to side at base

Safety Rules:

  • Stay LOW (heat and smoke rise)
  • Keep exit behind you - never let fire get between you and exit
  • Use correct extinguisher type:
    • RED (Water) - Paper, wood, cloth
    • BLACK (CO2) - Electrical fires
    • CREAM (Foam) - Flammable liquids
    • BLUE (Powder) - General purpose
  • If fire does NOT go out in 10 seconds - EVACUATE
NEVER use water on electrical or oil fires. If you empty one extinguisher and fire continues, LEAVE IMMEDIATELY.

• Use emergency stairs - NEVER elevators
  • Close doors behind you (slows fire spread)
  • Stay low if smoke present
  • Feel doors before opening (hot = fire on other side, use alternate route)
  • If caught in smoke: Drop to hands and knees, breathe through cloth
  • Go to designated assembly point outside
  • Do NOT re-enter for any reason
If trapped: Go to room with window, close door, seal cracks with wet cloth, signal from window. Call 997 and tell them your exact location.

At Assembly Point:

  • Direct evacuees to safe distance (minimum 50 meters from building)
  • Take headcount if you have personnel roster
  • Ask if anyone is missing or still inside
  • Keep people calm and together
  • Prevent anyone from re-entering building
  • Direct Civil Defense to exact fire location upon arrival
  • Inform Civil Defense of any known trapped persons

After emergency is controlled:

  • Create incident report in GuardLink system
  • Document timeline of events
  • List all emergency service units that responded
  • Note any injuries or property damage
  • Collect witness statements
  • Take photos of damage (if safe and authorized)
  • Notify client/management with preliminary report
  • Cooperate with Civil Defense investigation
To conduct systematic security patrols ensuring all areas are monitored and irregularities are detected and reported.
All guards assigned to patrol duties at client projects.

Purpose

Systematic patrols deter criminal activity, identify hazards, and ensure site security. GuardLink's checkpoint scanning system ensures accountability and proof of patrol completion.

Patrol Types

  • Routine Patrol: Scheduled regular rounds
  • Random Patrol: Unpredictable timing to prevent pattern recognition
  • Response Patrol: Investigating specific incident or alarm
To ensure all security incidents are accurately documented, reported promptly, and properly escalated.
All security personnel must report incidents using GuardLink Incident Management module.

What is an Incident?

Any event that:

  • Threatens safety or security
  • Violates laws, regulations, or site policies
  • Causes or could cause injury, damage, or loss
  • Requires documentation for legal or insurance purposes

Incident Categories

  • Theft / Loss of Property
  • Assault / Violence
  • Medical Emergency
  • Fire / Hazmat
  • Trespassing / Unauthorized Access
  • Vandalism / Property Damage
  • Suspicious Activity
  • Safety Hazard

The 5 W's of Incident Reporting

  • WHO: All persons involved (names, descriptions, contact info)
  • WHAT: Exactly what happened (facts only, no opinions)
  • WHEN: Precise date and time
  • WHERE: Exact location (building, floor, room)
  • WHY: Apparent cause or reason (if known)
